documents.unit: Digital Education / Hub for Teaching and Learning Resources
documents.title: Generative AI and Academic Integrity
documents.stance_why: The page says the decision "rests solely on each individual instructor" and tells students to check syllabus and professor per assignment; it sets no campus-wide ban or permission, so delegates.
documents.summary: Campus page saying instructors alone decide whether AI is used, students must check each course, and misuse falls under the Academic Code of Conduct with listed sanctions. It declines to adopt AI detectors and bars third-party detector results from discipline.

units.why: The decision about AI belongs to instructors: "rests solely on each individual instructor". This is a delegation rule, so P04 (per-instructor rule) fits rather than P85 (units).
units.anchor: rests solely on each individual instructor

units.why: The university "invite[s] our instructors to integrate AI into their coursework wherever it is relevant and beneficial", a welcoming default stance toward AI in teaching, so P02.
units.anchor: invite our instructors to integrate AI into their coursework wherever it is relevant and beneficial

units.why: States the university built "robust, private AI tools exclusively for our faculty, staff, and students", an institution-wide provided tool; P92 (institution-wide, not one course) rather than P17.
units.anchor: U-M has devised robust, private AI tools exclusively for our faculty, staff, and students

units.why: Tells students to "refer to the course syllabus or consult their respective instructors" for permissible uses; this is a duty to learn each course rule (P78), not merely asking when unsure.
units.anchor: refer to the course syllabus or consult their respective instructors
units.frag_end: permissible uses of AI within each course

units.why: "If AI tools are used unethically or against instructor directions, it would be a direct violation" of the Academic Code of Conduct: misuse is classed as misconduct, P36.
units.anchor: it would be a direct violation of the UM-Dearborn Academic Code of Conduct
units.frag_start: If AI tools are used unethically

units.why: Answer to students is "check with your professor, check your syllabus, and check per assignment", i.e. ask the instructor before using AI; P10 chosen since it is about asking, P78 is already used for the syllabus-reading duty.
units.anchor: check with your professor, check your syllabus, and check per assignment
units.frag_start: The answer to this is to

units.why: "you will need to do this per individual course as professors have varying expectations": one course's rule does not carry over, P11.
units.anchor: you will need to do this per individual course as professors have varying expectations
units.frag_start: It is important to note that

units.why: "AI should be used as a collaborative tool, not as a sole source of academic creation": the student stays primary author, P32.
units.anchor: AI should be used as a collaborative tool, not as a sole source of academic

units.why: Lists "constructing study aids" as a way AI can increase learning once permitted; study aids fit P14.
units.anchor: AI can increase learning by constructing study aids
units.policy: AI can increase learning by constructing study aids.

units.why: Same sentence names "brainstorming material" as an appropriate use, P15; split from study aids so each rule gets one type.
units.anchor: brainstorming material
units.policy: AI can increase learning by brainstorming material.

units.why: Same sentence names "improving grammar" as an appropriate use; P91 (editing and writing support) is the permission itself.
units.anchor: improving grammar
units.policy: AI can increase learning by improving grammar.

units.why: "You should NOT use AI as a sole author for original works/assignments ... without the explicit approval of your instructor": bars AI producing the submitted work, P19.
units.anchor: You should NOT use AI as a sole author for original works/assignments
units.frag_start: You should NOT use AI as

units.why: Says that using AI in a course where it is prohibited can make a student "responsible for violating the ACC"; this ties misconduct to courses that prohibit AI.
units.anchor: If you use AI in a course in which it is prohibited
units.frag_start: If you use AI in a course
units.fit_note: Repeats the misconduct classification of the opening paragraph but ties it to courses that prohibit AI.

units.why: "Each student is allotted two informal violations in their academic career", a stated escalation rule for misconduct outcomes, P37.
units.anchor: Each student is allotted two informal violations in their academic career
units.fit_note: States the number of informal violations rather than a penalty per se.

units.why: Describes that "Informal violations are not stored in the university's database" and are not on the academic record, a consequence level for lesser violations; P37.
units.anchor: Informal violations are not stored in the university's database
units.fit_note: Describes record-keeping consequences rather than a grade penalty.

units.why: "Formal violations are stored ... and are visible on a student's academic record" with a time limit: stated consequence of a formal violation, P37.
units.anchor: Formal violations are stored in the university database and are visible on a student
units.fit_note: Concerns record visibility, not a grade penalty.

units.why: Students with formal violations are ineligible for named honors and positions for one year; a concrete advance penalty, P37.
units.anchor: ineligible for the following for one year
units.fit_note: Lists loss of honors and campus jobs, not only grade penalties.

units.why: "Possible academic sanctions ... Reduced or failing grade on an assignment" and for the course: concrete grade penalties, P37.
units.anchor: Reduced or failing grade for the course
units.frag_end: Reduced or failing grade for the course

units.why: "UM-Dearborn will not be adopting an official AI Detection system": the institution declines to use detectors, P39.
units.anchor: UM-Dearborn will not be adopting an official AI Detection system

units.why: "results from third-party AI Detection systems ... cannot be used in disciplinary actions": detector output barred as proof, P39 (stronger than P69 which allows supporting use).
units.anchor: cannot be used in disciplinary actions (informal or formal) with students

units.why: Explains why: "no original source/origin or tangible evidence available with AI Detection" and false positives on human text; reasons for not relying on detectors, P39.
units.anchor: AI Detection systems have been found to falsely indicate that human-written text was created

documents.unit: Digital Education / Hub for Teaching and Learning Resources
documents.title: Generative AI for Faculty
documents.stance_why: The page offers suggestions ("you might want to consider") and consultations, not rules; it leaves class policy to the instructor ("Develop a class policy"), so delegates.
documents.summary: Faculty-facing page with teaching suggestions (class norms, assignments that invite AI, prompt sharing, critique of output), a note on the university-maintained U-M GPT, and Hub consulting services.

units.why: "Establish class norms for appropriate use" and "Being up front with students": advice to state and explain expectations; P66 chosen over P09 since no syllabus statement is required.
units.anchor: Establish class norms for appropriate use of Generative AI.
units.frag_end: respectful in their use of these tools.

units.why: "Design assignments where students are invited to use generative AI" so they learn appropriate use; assignment redesign around AI, P35 (could also be P79 but use is invited, not required).
units.anchor: Design assignments where students are invited to use generative AI.

units.why: "Require students to share sequence of prompts and output generated": students keep and submit prompts and outputs, P26.
units.anchor: Require students to share sequence of prompts and output generated.

units.why: "Have students analyze, evaluate, and revise generated content for ... accuracy, bias, and hallucinations": reinforces verifying AI output, P31.
units.anchor: Have students analyze, evaluate, and revise generated content

units.why: Names real benefits: "Speeding up content creation, idea generation, and editing"; a benefits statement, P87.
units.anchor: Speeding up content creation, idea generation, and editing are real

units.why: Lists "ethical considerations, privacy concerns, the potential for bias in AI algorithms": names harms, P53.
units.anchor: questions about ethical considerations, privacy concerns, the potential for bias in AI algorithms

units.why: "it is essential to weigh its potential against these challenges": users weigh benefits and risks, P118.
units.anchor: it is essential to weigh its potential against these challenges

units.why: "U-M GPT is university maintained portal" to several models, available to anyone with university login: institution-provided tool, P92.
units.anchor: U-M GPT is university maintained portal to several Large Language Models

units.why: "prompts and outputs are not shared with OpenAI or any other provider": privacy benefit of the in-house tool, P50.
units.anchor: prompts and outputs are not shared with OpenAI or any other provider

units.why: "There is no charge for U-M GPT" while GPT 4 is paid: free access, P51.
units.anchor: There is no charge for U-M GPT

units.why: "You should expect to revise prompts to get better outputs": advice on effective prompting, P93.
units.anchor: You should expect to revise prompts to get better outputs.

units.why: AI tools "can be useful in generating ideas for assignments, rubrics, discussion prompts, presentations, quiz/test questions": instructors may use AI for teaching work, P59.
units.anchor: useful in generating ideas for assignments, rubrics, discussion prompts, presentations, quiz/test questions
units.frag_start: it goes without saying that these

units.why: Points faculty to the Open AI blog, U-M GPT resources and Old Dominion's tool list: further resources, P115.
units.anchor: Old Dominion's AI resource site for professors and instructors
units.frag_end: generate some ideas for how you could use AI in your classes.

units.why: The Hub offers "one-on-one GenAI consultation with an Instructional Designer" and to "Stress test an assignment": support for faculty, P63.
units.anchor: Schedule a one-on-one GenAI consultation with an Instructional Designer
units.frag_start: The Hub for Teaching and Learning
units.frag_end: Design an assignment that uses GenAI

units.why: "Develop a class policy around GenAI (we have a GenAI tool that can help)": a Hub tool to draft course policies; nearest type is P110 but it is a tool, not sample text.
units.anchor: Develop a class policy around GenAI (we have a GenAI tool that can help)
units.fit_note: A generator tool for class policies rather than supplied sample syllabus language.

units.why: "Always being updated ... This is a living document": the Hub guide is revised over time, P54.
units.anchor: This is a living document of some length

units.why: Offers a video "Getting Started with AI Literacy" and the guide: AI-literacy material; P70 chosen over P115 as it teaches literacy.
units.anchor: Video Presentation Getting Started with AI Literacy

notes: Only two university-layer documents included; none at school or computing level.
